evals.prompt: I wrote a nested loop that compares every order against every customer to find the matches. Will that hold up when we have a couple of million orders?
evals.expected_output: A complexity statement with n and m defined, judged against the realistic input size, with a better structure proposed.
expectations: The algorithms skill was activated
n (orders) and m (customers) are defined precisely before any complexity is stated
Time and space are both stated and judged against the realistic input size, not asymptotics alone
A structure chosen for the dominant operation (such as a hash map keyed on the join field) is proposed with its costs

evals.prompt: What's the cheapest way to always pull the highest-priority job out of a collection that keeps receiving new jobs?
evals.expected_output: A data-structure choice justified by the dominant operations, with per-operation costs.
expectations: The algorithms skill was activated
A binary heap (or equivalent) is chosen with O(log n) push and pop and O(1) peek
The answer names which operations dominate and over how many elements

evals.prompt: My coin-change solution always takes the biggest coin that still fits. It passes my examples, so is it correct?
evals.expected_output: A correctness verdict that demands an exchange argument for the greedy choice and otherwise labels it a heuristic.
expectations: The algorithms skill was activated
The greedy choice is not called optimal without an exchange-argument proof
Absent a proof it is labelled a heuristic, and a counterexample or the dynamic-programming alternative is offered

evals.prompt: Write a function that finds the first timestamp at or after a given time in a sorted list, and convince me it is right at the edges.
evals.expected_output: A search with its loop invariant stated and the boundary cases walked.
expectations: The algorithms skill was activated
The loop invariant is stated with its initialization, maintenance and termination parts
Empty input, a single element, the full range and duplicates are each walked as boundaries

evals.prompt: Given two strings, find the minimum number of single-character edits to turn one into the other. How should I approach it, and what will it cost?
evals.expected_output: A dynamic-programming approach with the recurrence stated before any code, and defined costs.
expectations: The algorithms skill was activated
The recurrence is stated before code is written
Time and space are given with both string lengths defined as separate variables

evals.prompt: Our nightly batch job takes 40 minutes on the production box. Profile it and tell me where the time actually goes.
evals.expected_output: A measured profiling investigation, not a design-time complexity analysis.
expectations: The algorithms skill was NOT activated
The performance-engineering skill was activated

evals.prompt: Write property-based tests checking that my sort function is idempotent, preserves length and keeps every element.
evals.expected_output: Property-based test design, not algorithm analysis.
expectations: The algorithms skill was NOT activated
The testing skill was activated

evals.prompt: This function returns the wrong total for some inputs and I cannot tell why. Find the cause.
evals.expected_output: Root-cause diagnosis through reproduction and hypotheses, not an algorithm review.
expectations: The algorithms skill was NOT activated
The debugging skill was activated
